skill.displayName: Alibabacloud Tech Solution Animation Creation Auto Deploy

llm.summary: This skill is coherent as an Alibaba Cloud auto-deployer, but it handles live credentials and IAM in unsafe, broad, and persistent ways.

dimensions.detail: The workflow uses live Alibaba Cloud credentials to create cost-incurring resources, pass a raw API key into deployment configuration, and publish the app at a public plaintext HTTP URL.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden local persistence or installer backdoor was found, but the runtime depends on Aliyun CLI auto plugin installation, plugin updates, and unpinned external CLI/template behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions emphasize automatic execution with no manual input, including high-impact IAM changes, key creation, deployment from a mutable remote Devs template, and public domain creation without an explicit approval gate.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The created API key, attached system policies, role trust-policy changes, bucket, project, functions, and custom domain can persist after the run; cleanup deletes some resources but does not remove policy grants or restore an existing role trust policy.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to auto-deploy an animation app, and most cloud actions fit that goal, but the workflow also creates a Bailian API key, grants account-wide OSS and FC policies, modifies a fixed RAM role trust policy, and exposes a public HTTP endpoint.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Run it only in a dedicated Alibaba Cloud account or tightly scoped deployment identity, avoid shared terminals or logs because it prints a live API key, verify the Devs template before deployment, and plan manual cleanup of the API key, IAM policy grants, role trust changes, public domain, functions, project, and OSS bucket.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Bailian key creation is disclosed and related to the app architecture, but printing the full key and combining it with broad cloud automation is not proportionate.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact says credentials should not be printed, yet the workflow later states and implements printing the full Bailian API key value.
[SDI-2] expected: Creating a Bailian API key is part of the deployment design, but the key appears long-lived and cleanup is manual rather than automatically enforced.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The create-api-key script prints API_KEY directly to stdout, which is unnecessary for deployment and can expose the secret in logs or transcripts.
[T05] unexpected: Some IAM authority is needed, but automatically attaching AliyunOSSFullAccess and AliyunFCFullAccess to the current RAM user and replacing a fixed role trust policy are broader and more persistent than the specific app deployment requires.
[T08] expected: Using a Devs template is central to the skill, but the template is referenced by mutable name without version or digest pinning before receiving the API key and role ARN.
[T09] unexpected: The API key stdout exposure is confirmed in the script and is not required for the stated purpose.
[T09] expected: A public endpoint is expected for an app demo, but the custom domain is HTTP-only, wildcard-routed, and permits broad methods, so users should treat it as exposed and cost-incurring.
[TM1] expected: Deleting the generated OSS bucket is a normal cleanup action, but the forced recursive deletion relies on the bucket variable being correct and lacks an extra confirmation or ownership check.
[SC2] expected: The reviewed curl calls contact a domain-registration service for token and DNS setup rather than executing downloaded code; the material supply-chain concern is better represented by the mutable Devs template.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill depends on broad shell and Alibaba Cloud CLI authority without a tight permission boundary or scoped role manifest.
[EA2] expected: Automation is the advertised purpose, but the automatic IAM, credential, deployment, and public exposure steps are high-impact enough to need stronger user control.
